newsitem.title: USA: U.S. renewable energy demand to slip - EIA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. renewable energy demand to slip - EIA.

text.p: U.S. demand for renewable energy should slip by 5.2 percent in 1997 to 6.9 million quadrillion Btu from 1996's 7.275 quadrillion, the Energy Information Administration said Friday.
In 1998, demand for renewable energy may ease slightly to 6.877 quadrillion Btu, the EIA said in its short-term outlook.

Renewable use jumped 6.2 percent in 1996 -- to account for about 7.7 percent of total domestic gross energy demand -- because of an increase in hydroelectric generation because of heavy rainfall, it said.
But the outlook said hydropower generation by electric utilities is expected to decrease in 1997 and 1998 from high 1996 levels because of an assumed normal streamflow in the Pacific Northwest.
However the Pacific Northwest has had heavy precipitation and flooding so far this winter.
